question: Which plants are included in Thallophyta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ulva, Chara and Cladophora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Thallophyta 

 
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are commonly called algae.
 
 

 
• Ulva is a small genus of marine and brackish water green algae.

 
 
• It is edible and is often called Sea Lettuce.
 
 
 
• Chara is a genus of charophyte green algae.
 
 
• They are multicellular and resemble land plants because of stem-like and leaf-like structures, and are found in freshwater.
 
 
 
• Cladophora is algae that belong to the class Ulvophyceae.
 
 
• It grows both in fresh and saline water.
 
• It has many nuclei present in its coenocytic body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bryophyta

 
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta
 
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves, apart from having a specialized tissue for conduction.
 
 
 
• Gymnosperms
 
 
• Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds.
 
 
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
• Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants. Seeds develop inside tissues that get modified to form the fruit of the plant.
